title: P256 TBZ/BFI inline emission, 2^24 candidate cap and UBFX scan dispatch on the DONE/first-operand-reuse base

claims.statement: For the protected full-production P256 target, the cold classical algorithm in proof.md and supporting documents recovers the scalar with probability at least0.39 using at most97305995997780574860429328243930244841472 scalar instruction equivalents, below2^126.193868217480510 group units at C1000. q1=377471100,q2=2^28,N=2^70. Includes construction, normalization, range-tree control, capped carry/failure costs, fixed block-window transport with hop1 transaction-bound ACK and hop2 DONE-flag completion, grouping, resolution, verification and output. Peak memory below2^136bytes; preprocessing below2^118units included; no advice or auxiliary powers. Analytical bound under the stated ideal-coin blocking-port machine, not production execution or formal certification. Hop2 DONE markers plus per-phase STLR signaling awaited via the barrier LDAXR/WFE primitive replace per-message acknowledgment and sender in-flight updates (16/12 receiver, 93/4 per potential record); the receive window is released only by the final flag load after all five packet words are in registers, so no mid-read publication can overwrite a packet; the first backward multiply preserves its low operand limbs and the second multiply omits their reload; each inline record emission uses one TBZ full-window test on8192-byte-stride windows and two BFI field inserts in place of mask/add/or/test/branch (2505/4 per incidence, +1 per flush firing in the hop1 row); the candidate cap is2^24 with its Markov loss charged and q1 re-optimized; the range scan forms its dispatch index with one UBFX (25 per range); DONE publication/handling/wait in a separate fixed row.

experiments.purpose: Check direction/carry-specialized assembly and descriptor invariants.
